S1.label: bug
S1.suggestionContent: WHAT: `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` is read without optional chaining, and mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined when evt.destinationCalendar is null or empty. WHY: any Google Meet booking where neither the organizer nor the event type has a destination calendar throws a TypeError, and booking creation fails. The old code used `?.`. HOW: use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

S2.label: bug
S2.suggestionContent: WHAT: references for non-calendar results (video) now get `credentialId: undefined`, where they used to get result.credentialId. WHY: handleCancelBooking only deletes video meetings when the video reference has a credentialId, so Zoom/Daily meetings are no longer deleted on cancel. HOW: keep result.credentialId for every result type.

S3.label: bug
S3.suggestionContent: WHAT: the fallback only runs when externalCalendarId is falsy, but it then searches for `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId`, so it never matches a real calendar. WHY: the calendar id becomes undefined, which drops the old fallback to destinationCalendar.externalId and sends updates for legacy references to the wrong calendar or makes them fail. HOW: fall back to the first destination calendar's externalId.

S4.label: bug
S4.suggestionContent: WHAT: the deleteEvent fallback searches for `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` only when externalCalendarId is falsy, so it always returns undefined. WHY: for references without externalCalendarId, the destination calendar fallback is lost and the delete falls back to the default calendar. If the event lives in a different calendar, it is left behind. HOW: use `event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId`.

S5.label: bug
S5.suggestionContent: WHAT: destinationCalendar is set to null when neither the event type nor the organizer has one, so `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` does nothing. WHY: in collective events where the first host has no destination calendar, the other hosts' calendars are silently dropped, which is the case this PR is supposed to fix. HOW: default to `[]` instead of null.

S6.label: bug
S6.suggestionContent: WHAT: createEvent always uses destinationCalendar[0].externalId. createAllCalendarEvents now calls it once per host credential, so every host's Office365 credential gets the first host's calendar id. WHY: a second collective host using Office365 posts to `/me/calendars/<host1-calendar-id>/events`, which does not exist in their account, so their event creation fails. HOW: pick the destination entry whose credentialId matches this credential, as GoogleCalendarService does.

S7.label: bug
S7.suggestionContent: WHAT: the recurring-series branch, which deletes the events of all updatedBookings for every user calendar credential, now sits inside the per-reference loop. WHY: with multiple calendar references, the same recurring events get one delete call per reference, which causes duplicate API calls and 404/410 errors. HOW: move the recurring deletion out of the reference loop so it runs once.

S8.label: bug
S8.suggestionContent: WHAT: the slug condition was flipped from `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` to `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED`. WHY: with billing enabled, the slug is set right away and also stored as requestedSlug, and with billing disabled, organizations are created with no slug. HOW: restore the negation.

S9.label: bug
S9.suggestionContent: WHAT: the catch block turns the plain Error thrown for an empty or invalid dynamicUserList into a generic 500 'Unable to load users'. WHY: a client input error comes back as a server error with its message hidden. HOW: throw `new HttpError({ statusCode: 400, ... })` directly for the validation failure.

S10.label: bug
S10.suggestionContent: `mainHostDestinationCalendar` comes from `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []`, so it is `undefined` when there is no destination calendar. Callers now pass `[]` or `null` in that case. A Google Meet booking without a destination calendar then throws a TypeError on `.integration` instead of falling back to Cal Video.

S11.label: bug
S11.suggestionContent: The `find` fallback only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, but it searches for a calendar whose `externalId` equals that same falsy value. It therefore never returns the event's destination calendar, and the update goes out with an undefined calendarId instead of the destination calendar used before this PR.

S12.label: bug
S12.suggestionContent: When neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, `destinationCalendar` is set to `null`. The following `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` then does nothing, so collective team members' calendars are silently discarded. Initializing it to an empty array keeps them.

S13.label: bug
S13.suggestionContent: When there is no destination calendar, handleNewBooking now passes `destinationCalendar: null` and other callers pass `[]`. `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` then leaves `mainHostDestinationCalendar` undefined, so reading `.integration` throws a TypeError. Every Google Meet booking without a destination calendar fails instead of falling back to Cal Video; using `?.integration` keeps the old fallback.

S14.label: bug
S14.suggestionContent: When evt.destinationCalendar is null or [] (handleNewBooking sets null when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar), mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined. `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` then throws a TypeError for every Google Meet booking. This breaks booking creation in the very case the Cal Video fallback is meant to handle.

S15.label: bug
S15.suggestionContent: `destinationCalendar` is now an array, and when it is null or empty (handleNewBooking passes null if no event-type or organizer calendar is set), `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is undefined. The old code read `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`, which handled null. The new code reads `.integration` on undefined, so every such booking throws a TypeError in EventManager.create. The fix is optional chaining on `mainHostDestinationCalendar`.

S16.label: bug
S16.suggestionContent: This branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, but it searches `destinationCalendar` for `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` using that same falsy value. The search never matches, so `selectedCalendar` is undefined. Before this change, the code fell back to the destination calendar's externalId.

S17.label: security
S17.suggestionContent: The new catch block in loadUsers copies `error.message` from `PrismaClientKnownRequestError` into a 400 HttpError, which this public, unauthenticated booking endpoint sends back to the caller. Prisma error messages can include model, field and constraint names and query details, which exposes internal database structure. Log the Prisma error on the server and return a generic message to the client.

S18.label: security
S18.suggestionContent: For COLLECTIVE events, every team member's full DestinationCalendar row (credentialId, externalId, userId) is now pushed into `evt.destinationCalendar`. `evt` is spread into the webhook payload, so other members' calendar IDs (often email addresses) and their credential IDs are sent to the webhook subscriber. Keep the team members' calendars off `evt`, for example by passing them to EventManager separately, or remove the field before building the payload.

S19.label: bug
S19.suggestionContent: The old code set `slug` only when team billing was disabled. The rewrite sets it only when billing is enabled, the same condition as `requestedSlug`. With billing enabled, orgs now get a final slug before payment or verification. With billing disabled, they get no slug at all.

S20.label: bug
S20.suggestionContent: The else branch runs only when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, yet it looks for `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId`. That can never match a real calendar, so the destination calendar fallback is dead code and `selectedCalendar` is always undefined. The same expression appears in deleteEvent (lines 315-317). The fallback should pick the destination calendar that belongs to this credential, or the main host's calendar.

S21.label: bug
S21.suggestionContent: The old code used `result.credentialId` for non-calendar (video) results. The new ternary returns `undefined` for them, so video references are stored without the credential that created the meeting. Later updates and deletes of those meetings can no longer find the right credential.

S22.label: bug
S22.suggestionContent: `destinationCalendar` falls back to `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has one. In that case `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` does nothing, and the destination calendars of the other collective hosts are thrown away. Initializing to an empty array keeps those team calendars.

S1.label: bug
S1.suggestionContent: WHAT: isTeamAdminOrOwner uses `&&` between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner, and isTeamAdmin already matches ADMIN or OWNER roles, so the check passes only for OWNERs. WHY: Team ADMINs who are not the organizer or an attendee get FORBIDDEN, even though the variable name says admins should be allowed. HOW: Use `||`, or just call isTeamAdmin, which already covers owners.

S2.label: bug
S2.suggestionContent: WHAT: sendAddGuestsEmails gets the raw `guests` input instead of the filtered `uniqueGuests`. WHY: An already-existing attendee who appears in the submitted list is treated as a new guest and gets a 'new booking scheduled' email instead of the 'guests added' notice. HOW: Pass `uniqueGuests`.

S3.label: bug
S3.suggestionContent: WHAT: EventManager is built from the caller's (ctx.user) credentials, but updateCalendarAttendees updates the booking references that live in the organizer's calendar. WHY: When an attendee or team owner adds guests, the calendar update runs with credentials that don't own those events, so the organizer's calendar event never gets the new attendees, or the update throws. HOW: Build EventManager from booking.user and that user's credentials, as other booking handlers do.

S4.label: bug
S4.suggestionContent: WHAT: updateCalendarAttendees runs after attendees are already saved to the database, and it is not wrapped in error handling. WHY: If the calendar provider call fails, the client gets an error but the guests stay saved without emails, and a retry is rejected with 'emails_must_be_unique_valid'. HOW: Wrap the calendar update in try/catch and log the error so emails still go out and the mutation reports success.

S5.label: security
S5.suggestionContent: WHAT: Blacklist entries are lowercased, but each guest email is compared with its original casing. WHY: Submitting a blacklisted address with any uppercase letter (e.g. `Bad@x.com`) gets past BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS and the address is added and emailed. HOW: Lowercase the guest before comparing it to the blacklist and to existing attendees.

S6.label: bug
S6.suggestionContent: WHAT: The server schema accepts duplicate emails in `guests`, and the handler only removes guests that are already attendees, not repeats within the input. WHY: A direct API call with the same email twice inserts duplicate attendee rows via createMany, because the uniqueness check exists only on the client. HOW: Add a refine that rejects duplicates (or dedupe with a Set in the handler).

S7.label: security
S7.suggestionContent: WHAT: `guests` has no maximum length, and any booking attendee is allowed to call the mutation. WHY: An authenticated attendee can submit thousands of arbitrary addresses in one request, and each one gets a calendar-invite email sent in the organizer's name, which turns this endpoint into a spam relay. HOW: Cap the array size (e.g. `.max(10)`), on top of rate limiting.

S8.label: security
S8.suggestionContent: The blacklist entries are lowercased (line 71), but the incoming guest email is compared without normalisation, so `includes(guest)` misses any mixed-case version of a blacklisted address. An attacker can add a blacklisted guest by changing the case of a few letters (e.g. `Spam@Domain.com`). Lowercase the guest before the blacklist comparison.

S9.label: bug
S9.suggestionContent: sendAddGuestsEmails in email-manager.ts assumes `newGuests` lists only newly added attendees and sends them the full AttendeeScheduledEmail invite. The handler instead passes the raw `guests` input, which can include emails that were already attendees. Those existing attendees then get a fresh booking confirmation instead of the add-guests notice; passing `uniqueGuests` fixes this.

S10.label: bug
S10.suggestionContent: Only the client dialog checks that guest emails are unique; the server schema accepts duplicates. The handler only removes guests who are already attendees, so a request like ["a@x.com","a@x.com"] creates two Attendee rows for the same email, because the Attendee table has no unique constraint. Enforce uniqueness on the server, for example by de-duplicating in the handler or adding a refine to the schema.

S11.label: bug
S11.suggestionContent: The handler filters the guests against an attendee list it read earlier, then calls createMany, with no transaction and no unique constraint on (bookingId, email). Two concurrent addGuests requests for the same booking can both pass the filter and insert the same guest twice. Re-check existing attendees inside a transaction, or add a unique constraint and use skipDuplicates.

S12.label: bug
S12.suggestionContent: sendAddGuestsEmails is passed the raw `guests` input instead of `uniqueGuests`. Guests that were filtered out because they were already attendees still receive the new-booking (AttendeeScheduledEmail) email instead of the guests-added email.

S13.label: bug
S13.suggestionContent: The variable is named isTeamAdminOrOwner, but it is only true when the user passes both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner. A team admin who is not an owner therefore gets FORBIDDEN. Use || to match the intent.

S14.label: bug
S14.suggestionContent: The handler builds uniqueGuests by dropping existing attendees and blacklisted emails, but sendAddGuestsEmails is called with the original `guests`. Any existing attendee included in the input is treated as a new guest and gets a fresh 'scheduled' email instead of the 'guests added' notice. Pass uniqueGuests.

S15.label: bug
S15.suggestionContent: blacklistedGuestEmails is lowercased, but each guest is compared exactly as entered. A blacklisted address typed with any uppercase letters gets past the filter. Lowercase the guest email before comparing.

S16.label: bug
S16.suggestionContent: The booking is loaded with user.credentials, but EventManager is built from ctx.user and that user's own credentials. When an attendee or team admin adds guests, the update to the organizer's calendar event runs with the wrong user's credentials and will not find the event or will fail. Build EventManager from booking.user and its credentials.

S17.label: bug
S17.suggestionContent: The tooltip text "Remove email" is hard-coded in English. The rest of the component translates its text through t() from useLocale (for example t("add_another")), so users in other languages see this one string in English. Use a translation key instead.

S18.label: bug
S18.suggestionContent: The variable is named isTeamAdminOrOwner, but the code joins the isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner checks with &&, so it is only true when both pass. Code that trusts the name will assume admins without the owner role are allowed. Use || so the logic matches the name.

S19.label: bug
S19.suggestionContent: The message is built with a template literal that always contains text, so `message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` never uses the translated fallback. When err.data.code or err.message is missing, users see raw text like "undefined: " instead of the localized error.

S20.label: bug
S20.suggestionContent: The comment "These are like 40kb" appears to be copied from the phone input lazy loader. MultiEmail only uses existing UI components, so the size claim misleads readers about why it is lazy-loaded.

S1.label: bug
S1.suggestionContent: WHAT: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the zod SafeParse result object, and that object is written directly as credential.key. WHY: the DB key becomes {success, data}, so googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key) at line 75 throws for every later request and the Google credential becomes unusable after the first refresh. HOW: store the parsed data.

S2.label: bug
S2.suggestionContent: WHAT: when credential sync is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, but this code reads res?.data as if it were a Gaxios response. WHY: token is undefined, so token.access_token throws a TypeError and Google tokens can never be refreshed in sync mode. HOW: in the sync branch, parse the Response JSON before using it, or make refreshOAuthTokens return the same shape that each caller expects.

S3.label: bug
S3.suggestionContent: WHAT: credentialId is passed where refreshOAuthTokens expects the credential's userId. WHY: the sync endpoint receives a credential id as calcomUserId, so it returns tokens for the wrong user or for none. HOW: pass the credential's userId instead.

S4.label: bug
S4.suggestionContent: WHAT: in sync mode, refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, but this code reads tokenInfo.data.error as if it were an axios response. WHY: tokenInfo.data is undefined, so the property access throws and the token refresh always fails when sync is enabled. HOW: await the Response's json() in the sync branch and use that value as the token data.

S5.label: bug
S5.suggestionContent: WHAT: both computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` evaluate to the literal property name '[object Object]', so the schema only declares access_token plus a field named '[object Object]'. WHY: zod strips every other field (expires_in, expiry_date, scope, token_type), so sync-mode refreshes lose expiry information and callers such as Zoom (expires_in) and office365 get NaN or missing values. HOW: use z.object({ access_token: z.string() }).passthrough(), with explicit optional expiry fields if needed.

S6.label: bug
S6.suggestionContent: WHAT: when the parsed response has no refresh_token, the code writes the literal string "refresh_token" into it. WHY: office365calendar spreads tokenResponse.data over the stored credentials (line 264), so a provider response without refresh_token (always the case with the stripping minimum schema) replaces the real stored refresh token with the string 'refresh_token', and the next refresh fails. HOW: remove the placeholder assignment so callers keep their existing refresh_token.

S7.label: bug
S7.suggestionContent: WHAT: the new code calls prisma.credential.update, but the file never imports prisma. Imports at lines 1-20 have no @calcom/prisma. WHY: this causes a TypeScript compile error or a ReferenceError at runtime, which rejects getClient so every Salesforce operation fails. HOW: add `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma";`.

S8.label: bug
S8.suggestionContent: WHAT: success is detected by comparing response.statusText to "OK". WHY: statusText is empty over HTTP/2 and in many fetch implementations, so successful refreshes throw a 400 and the Salesforce client can never be created. HOW: check response.ok instead.

S9.label: bug
S9.suggestionContent: WHAT: the token is refreshed and saved, but jsforce.Connection is still built with the old credentialKey.access_token and instance_url. WHY: the refresh result is discarded for the current connection, so requests use the stale or expired token. HOW: pass accessTokenParsed.data.access_token and accessTokenParsed.data.instance_url to the Connection.

S10.label: performance
S10.suggestionContent: WHAT: getClient runs on every SalesforceCalendarService construction and always makes a token refresh HTTP call plus a credential DB write, without checking whether the token is expired. WHY: this adds an external round-trip and a DB write to every booking or calendar operation, and frequent refreshes can hit Salesforce rate limits. HOW: refresh only when the token is invalid or expired, or rely on jsforce's built-in refresh handling.

S11.label: bug
S11.suggestionContent: WHAT: appStoreMetadata is indexed by app.slug, but the map is keyed by app directory name (see _appRegistry.ts:17, which uses app.dirName). WHY: for apps whose slug differs from their dirName (e.g. google-calendar vs googlecalendar), the lookup returns undefined and the webhook always responds 404, so those credentials cannot be synced. HOW: select dirName from prisma.app and index appStoreMetadata by it.

S12.label: security
S12.suggestionContent: WHAT: the webhook secret is checked with a plain !== string comparison. WHY: this endpoint can overwrite any user's third-party credentials, and a non-constant-time comparison exposes the secret to timing analysis. HOW: compare using crypto.timingSafeEqual on equal-length buffers after confirming the header is a string.

S13.label: security
S13.suggestionContent: WHAT: when state.teamId is present, the code only checks that the user is an accepted team member before creating a team credential, and throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam runs only on the path where teamId is falsy, so it is effectively a no-op. WHY: any non-admin team member can install OAuth apps on behalf of the team through a crafted state parameter. HOW: call throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam({ teamId: state.teamId, userId }) inside the teamId branch before prisma.credential.create.

S14.label: bug
S14.suggestionContent: WHAT: in sync mode, refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, but the result is used directly as a HubspotToken. WHY: expiresIn and accessToken are undefined on a Response, so expiryDate becomes NaN, a Response object is persisted as the credential key, and setAccessToken(undefined) is called. HOW: parse the Response JSON in the sync branch before treating it as a token.

S15.label: security
S15.suggestionContent: The webhook secret is checked with `!==`, which can leak timing information and let an attacker recover CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET byte by byte. Anyone with the secret can overwrite any user's app credentials. Compare in constant time with crypto.timingSafeEqual, after confirming the header is a string and the lengths match.

S16.label: security
S16.suggestionContent: `refreshOAuthTokens` gets `credentialId` (the Credential row id) as its `userId` argument. With credential sync enabled, it asks the sync endpoint for the tokens of the user whose id equals that credential id and saves them onto this credential. As a result, one user's Zoho Bigin access token is stored under another user's account and can be used by them; pass the credential owner's userId instead.

S17.label: bug
S17.suggestionContent: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a zod SafeParseReturn ({success, data}), but this code saves that whole object as credential.key. The stored Google credential then holds {success, data} instead of access_token/refresh_token/expiry_date, which breaks later reads. Persist `.data` instead.

S18.label: bug
S18.suggestionContent: refreshOAuthTokens declares its third parameter as userId and sends it to the sync endpoint as calcomUserId. This call passes credentialId instead, so in sync mode the endpoint is asked for tokens for the wrong (or a nonexistent) user. Pass the credential's userId instead.

S19.label: bug
S19.suggestionContent: When credential sync is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, but this code reads `res?.data` as if it were a googleapis response. That makes `token` undefined, so reading `token.access_token` throws and the refresh fails every time in sync mode. Parse the body with `await res.json()` when the sync path is used.

S20.label: bug
S20.suggestionContent: The comments say any numeric property is treated as the expiry and that other properties are allowed. In fact `z.string().toString()` evaluates to the literal key "[object Object]", so both lines define that one key and the second overrides the first. S21.label: bug
S21.suggestionContent: refreshOAuthTokens's third parameter is `userId` and is sent to the sync endpoint as `calcomUserId`, but here it receives the credential id. S22.label: bug

S23.label: bug
S23.suggestionContent: `refreshOAuthTokens` sends its third argument to the sync endpoint as `calcomUserId`, but this call passes `credentialId`. When credential sync is enabled, the endpoint gets tokens for an unrelated user, or for no user, and those tokens are used for this credential.

S1.label: bug
S1.suggestionContent: WHAT: The `retryCount > 1` branch of the deleteMany OR has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter, so the SMS cron deletes any WorkflowReminder (email or WhatsApp) whose retryCount is above 1. WHY: Once another cron starts incrementing retryCount, this job will silently delete reminders for other methods. HOW: Add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` to the retryCount condition.

S2.label: bug
S2.suggestionContent: WHAT: The new retryCount increment sits inside `if (message?.length && ... && sendTo)`, so a reminder with a missing phone number or an empty message never increments its counter. WHY: These reminders can never succeed, but they are still re-fetched and re-processed on every cron run until scheduledDate passes, which is the behavior the PR is meant to stop. HOW: Move the increment into an else branch of the outer `if` as well, or into one failure path that covers both cases.

S3.label: bug
S3.suggestionContent: WHAT: The prisma.workflowReminder.update added in the catch block has no guard, so if it throws (for example P2025 because the reminder was deleted, or a DB error), the exception escapes the for-loop. WHY: All remaining reminders in this cron run are skipped and the handler returns an error instead of continuing. HOW: Wrap the catch-block update in its own try/catch, or use updateMany, which does not throw when no row matches.

S4.label: bug
S4.suggestionContent: WHAT: Every failure from twilio.scheduleSMS increments retryCount, including temporary ones: an undefined return while the account is SMS-locked, a throw from checkSMSRateLimit when the monthly limit is hit, and Twilio network or 5xx errors. WHY: Two consecutive cron runs with a temporary failure permanently delete a valid reminder, so the attendee never gets the SMS even after the condition clears. HOW: Increment retryCount only for permanent errors, such as Twilio invalid-number error codes, and let temporary errors retry without counting.

S5.label: bug

S1.label: security

HOW: Require that the password was verified before accepting a backup code. For example, reject when `credentials.backupCode` is set and the password check did not run, or run verifyPassword unconditionally in the backup-code branch.

WHY: Two concurrent login requests with the same code both read the old list, both find the code, and both succeed, so a single-use code can authenticate multiple sessions. HOW: Make the update conditional on the previously read ciphertext (`updateMany({ where: { id: user.id, backupCodes: user.backupCodes }, ... })`) and reject the login if count is 0.

S3.label: bug

WHY: After that dismissal, viewer.me is never invalidated, so the switch stays unchecked even though 2FA is on. The next time the modal opens it starts on the stale backup-codes step instead of ConfirmPassword. HOW: Wrap onOpenChange so that closing while `step === SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes` calls resetState() and onEnable().

S4.label: bug

WHY: A user who types the code in uppercase, which the 'XXXXX-XXXXX' placeholder invites, gets IncorrectBackupCode and can be locked out of recovery. HOW: Normalize with `.toLowerCase()` before indexOf.

S7.label: bug

Make the write conditional on the ciphertext that was read (for example `updateMany` where `backupCodes` still equals the value read, and reject the login if the update count is 0), or run it in a serializable transaction.

WHY: <script> tags, event handlers or `javascript:` hrefs in feed or page content run in the Discourse origin wherever cooked is rendered (topic view and the embed iframe use `raw post.cooked`), which is stored XSS. HOW: run the raw HTML through the same whitelist sanitizer the normal pipeline uses (e.g. PrettyText's sanitize step) before returning it.

S2.label: security

WHY: a URL like `http://host/'onmouseover='alert(1)` is a valid URI and breaks out of the attribute, injecting an event handler into the imported post. HOW: escape the URL with ERB::Util.html_escape in both the attribute and the link text.

S3.label: security

WHY: an attacker can vary the query string or path on the embeddable host (`?a=1`, `?a=2`, ...) to get past the throttle and make the server create an unlimited number of topics as embed_by_username. HOW: throttle per client or globally rather than per URL, and normalize the URL (or drop the query string) before using it as the throttle key and embed key.

S4.label: performance
S4.suggestionContent: WHAT: For every embed URL that is not yet imported, perform_retrieve runs Jobs::PollFeed synchronously, which downloads the whole feed and runs TopicEmbed.import for every item. WHY: every retrieval for an unknown URL (which an anonymous caller can trigger repeatedly with distinct URLs) costs a full feed fetch with no timeout plus N import/SHA comparisons, so worker time grows with feed size × request rate. HOW: rely on the hourly scheduled poll, or cache the last poll time in Redis and skip the inline poll if one ran recently.

S5.label: bug

WHY: external links and images become `http://host/cdn.example.com/a.png`, which breaks them in every imported post. HOW: skip values that start with `//` (and do the same for img src).

S6.label: bug

WHY: the NoMethodError on nil aborts the whole poll (retry: false) and also aborts the inline poll inside TopicRetriever, so no items are imported. HOW: fall back to description and skip items that have no body.

S7.label: bug

WHY: when the feed content changes, `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!` raises NoMethodError, which aborts the feed poll for every remaining item. HOW: return early (or recreate the post) when embed.post is nil.

S8.label: bug

S9.suggestionContent: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin)` accepts any origin that is a substring of discourseUrl. For example, `https://forum.example.co` passes for `https://forum.example.com/`, so an attacker-controlled domain can send messages to the embedding page. S10.suggestionContent: The embed view formats dates with strftime("%e %b %Y"), which always gives English month abbreviations and a fixed day-month-year order. S11.label: security
S11.suggestionContent: The imported_from footer builds `#{url}` from a feed-supplied URL without escaping it. The post is cooked as raw_html, so this markup is shown to readers unchanged. A quote or `<` in the URL breaks out of the attribute and injects markup. Escape the URL with ERB::Util.html_escape before putting it into the HTML.

S12.label: bug
S12.suggestionContent: SimpleRSS sets `content` only from a `<content>` element; standard RSS 2.0 items only have `<description>`, so `i.content` is nil and `i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError. The error aborts the whole poll, so no items get imported, and it also propagates into TopicRetriever, which runs PollFeed synchronously. S13.label: bug
S13.suggestionContent: The code looks up `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and then creates the topic, post and embed, with no lock between the two steps. PollFeed, RetrieveTopic jobs (staff skip the throttle) and the Disqus importer can import the same URL at the same time. Both see no embed, and the second `create!` raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique on the unique `embed_url` index, which crashes that job and stops the rest of its feed loop. Rescue RecordNotUnique and fall back to the update path, or serialize imports per URL with a lock.

S14.label: bug
S14.suggestionContent: `start_with?('/')` also matches protocol-relative URLs such as `//cdn.example.com/img.png`, and `sub(/^\/+/, '')` strips both slashes, giving `http://eviltrout.com/cdn.example.com/img.png`. S15.label: security
S15.suggestionContent: `indexOf(e.origin) === -1` accepts any origin that appears anywhere in discourseUrl, including a shorter host that is a prefix, like `http://forum.example.co` for `http://forum.example.com/`. Messages from that origin are then trusted and can resize the iframe. Require discourseUrl to begin with the exact origin followed by `/`, or to equal it.

S16.label: security

Render the embed as anonymous (pass `nil` as the user) or skip public caching when a user is logged in.

S5.label: bug
